I am old, and my back is not what it used to be. But I still work my 4.1 mu with my own hands. My son is gone to the city, so it is just me and my husband now. This is how I farm this year, the same way I have always done it.

For wheat, I plant in October, after the maize comes off. I buy two bags of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind, fifty jin each, one bag for two mu, so I need about two bags for my land. I spread it when I plough. Then in spring, when I turn on the well water the first time, I scatter urea — half a bag per mu, about twenty-five jin. The seed I buy at the village shop, whatever kind the dealer says is good this year — everyone in the village plants the same kind. I water three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once in spring at green-up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray once for the red spider mite and once when I see the wheat aphids on the head. If the year is good I get 450 jin per mu, sometimes a little more.

For maize, I plant right after I cut the wheat, no ploughing — I just use the small rotary on the tractor my neighbor drives for me. The seed is hybrid, I buy it every year, you cannot save hybrid seed, even I know that. I put compound fertilizer in the row when I plant, about forty jin per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high I spread urea, about thirty jin per mu, and I water right after so it goes down to the roots. I water two times if the rain is normal, three times if it is dry. I spray once for the corn borer when I see the holes in the leaves. Maize gives me 500 jin per mu usually.

I do not like to use less fertilizer. One bad harvest and I have nothing. A few yuan of urea is nothing compared to losing the crop. My neighbors do about the same as me. That is how we know it works.
